A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the method presented in this paper is a robust, accurate and efficient way to segment subcortical regions from MR brain images, using only intensity information, and without the need for any prior tissue classification.
the Bayesian Active Shape and Appearance Model is a powerful tool for the automatic segmentation of subcortex from T1-weighted brain MR images, and is a useful tool for clinical research.

the method presented here provides a robust and reliable means for automatic subcortical segmentation of T1-weighted images and is capable of producing results comparable to manual segmentation, with the added benefit of being able to produce probabilistic measures of shape change.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Bayesian Active Appearance Model is a powerful and general framework for combining shape and intensity information in the context of image registration and segmentation.
it is possible to obtain good segmentation of subcortex from T1 images using a model that is trained on manually labelled training data.

the use of shape and appearance priors, combined within a Bayesian framework and trained using manually-labelled images, can provide useful information for automatic subcortical segmentation, and that this information can be used to provide a local, direct measure of geometric shape change in structure.
